heuristics: R: the one heuristic premise, the random-function idealization of the adder walk on classes. Each class's key, canonical fractions and orientation are i.i.d. uniform, independent of x and the coins, and the class map is algebraic on top of them. Every conditional statement used is a theorem of R by deferred decisions (proof.md section 2.2). L-ori, the uniform arriving sign with non-equal share 1/6, is a theorem of R (T2). The birthday count of section 2.1 is R's random-mapping count.

H3: Callgrind instruction counts on production inputs represent the common path: 808.67 (plain) and 818.66 (anchor) instructions per walk step, plus at most 2 for the canon_pick branch (C_COMMON = 821), with the rare paths out of line and charged at worst case; the Markov reserve covers the expected rare work.
limitations: R is measured only in marginal form: the non-equal share is 1/6 within 0.8 standard errors on fresh windows at A = 8 to 1024 (proof.md section 4, evidence/sign-law.json). The conditional laws are theorems of R, not measurements.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution. Needs about 2^67.7 stored distinguished points; not a practical attack.
All field arithmetic is the package's own inline assembly, tested against Python big integers but not formally verified.
R is an unproved heuristic, and the argument is not established at production size: the toy runs use theta = 2^-5, and the formal test uses 6 adder bits and theta = 2^-6.
The rare-path charges are forced-path maxima measured with a bounding build (proof.md section 8.1), checked for equality and dominance on the forced paths, not proved for every input.
The exact-k fallback rate (2^-55 per canon call, proof.md section 6) follows from R and is not measured, since no fallback occurred in the measured steps.
Escape depths are at most TRAIL_MAX (proof.md section 2.3); the order-of-2 check of section 2.4 needs no assumption beyond the assertions in accounting.py.
The replay cut-off (65n steps, REPLAY_FACTOR = 65) is in the core and the regenerated experiment.py; a cut-off replay fails the run and is counted in DELTA_CUT (proof.md sections 1.3 and 3).

The measurement harness takes restart starts from a precomputed pool of 1024 points (measurement/step.c); the specified algorithm draws fresh coins for every restart and is charged at its cost (proof.md section 2.5).
The model success bound is 0.411524 at tau = 0.5303, 0.0215 above 0.39; the pooled toy-curve success at that budget is in the evidence.
Distinguished points never occur in a production-parameter measurement sample; their restart and abandonment paths were checked on small builds.
The probe cost (2^11 per probe, L = 2^10, DP_COST = 2^21) and the draw cost (2^16 per draw) are allowances, not measurements (proof.md sections 8.2 and 10).
The useful-merge bound (proof.md section 2.8, Lemma M) is DELTA_NR, about 2^-46, in expectation under R; it replaces the earlier first-merge bound.

The sampling caps (D = 4 draws per scalar and attempts per point) and the probe cap (L = 2^10) abort the run; their probabilities are in delta (DELTA_CAP, DELTA_PROBE; proof.md sections 1.3 and 8.2). The toy experiment retries identity starts without a cap.

The meter's expectation, and so the 1/64, is taken in R. A model-free rare-work bound would charge the anchor check at its worst on every step, which costs about 10.9 bits (time_log2 about 137.4 instead of 126.5); it is not taken, and the work bound holds unconditionally on every run that does not abort.
